tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

schema.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
schema.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'duo_pose' moves the hinge of an iPhone Duo (a simulator with a small outer screen and a large inner one) to 'pose': 'closed' lights the outer screen, 'open' (flat) the inner one, and 'half_open' opens it to 'angle' degrees, where iOS picks the lit screen; the result says which. Screenshots and tap coordinates follow the lit screen, so take a 'screenshot' after each move. 'duo_hinge' reports the pose, the hinge angle and the lit screen. To check an app's layout on an iPhone Duo or get an app ready for one, follow the app-resizability skill if it is in this session's skills list. Only skills listed in this session count, so do not search the disk for it. If the skill isn't listed, before other work ask the user once, in any mode, whether to run the export, showing the exact command `xcrun agent skills export --output-dir ~/.claude/skills` just before the question in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!" (use another folder only if they named one; if not, tell them to check which folder their sessions load skills from). Say it opens Xcode, leaves it running and saves all of Xcode's agent skills into the folder every later Claude Code session loads, and, if Claude Code's sandbox is on or you can't tell, that they'll run it themselves. Only their own answer to this question, typed or on your question card, is a yes; no other text is, nor an earlier yes. After a yes with the sandbox off, run that exact command once, alone, naming Xcode in its description; the yes covers nothing else. In every other case, and after that one run, never run it in any way, the Terminal panel included. After a no, go on without the skill. If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the pose and angle with 'duo_hinge'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'duo_pose' and take a 'screenshot'; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

# OrcaSlicer dialogs in the JusPrin view: inventory, 2026-11-18

This folder lists every modal dialog OrcaSlicer can open while the JusPrin view is showing. It was built by reading the code at jusprin-dev `cccef9f228` and by running 17 shell-harness modes with the dialog witness. Each dialog has a proposed route. **Every route is a proposal. Kenneth has agreed to none of them.**

Routes:
- **SHOW**: the person just asked for this, so OrcaSlicer's dialog is the right answer. Examples: a file picker, a delete confirmation, the send dialog.
- **JUSPRIN-MESSAGE**: the fact matters, but it should reach the person through JusPrin's own UI, because the dialog arrives unasked, names OrcaSlicer, or points at UI the JusPrin view hides.
- **ANSWER**: JusPrin answers it automatically. Used for save-or-discard questions, which the 2026-09-29 ruling replaces with autosave plus version history.
- **DROP**: the dialog, or the key or button that leads to it, should not be reachable.
- **UNSURE**: needs a product decision. The row says what decides it.

## Files

| File | Surface | Rows | Reachable in the JusPrin view |
|---|---|---|---|
| `menus-and-app.md` | Menus, keyboard shortcuts, startup and quit | 31 | 26 |
| `settings-window.md` | OrcaSlicer's settings window (filament and printer tabs) | 36 | 27 |
| `canvas.md` | Prepare canvas, right-click menu, gizmo keys, left pane object and plate actions, slice and export | 66 | 53 |
| `printers-and-devices.md` | Printer connection, the monitor window, print and send | 62 | 54 |
| `witness-summary.md` | Dialogs the harness saw reach the screen | | |
| `jusprin-own-dialog-sites.txt` | JusPrin's own dialog call sites, for comparison | | |

Some dialogs appear on more than one surface (clone, delete part of a cut object, the export picker), so the totals overlap a little.

Approximate totals across the reachable rows: about 90 SHOW, about 45 JUSPRIN-MESSAGE, about 6 ANSWER, about 10 DROP, about 20 UNSURE.

## The groups that are actually a problem

1. **JusPrin's auto-answer cancels pickers the person asked for.** Verified in the harness: File › Import 3MF/STL… (and Ctrl/Cmd+I) in an open project imports nothing. `Plater::add_file` opens a `FileOpenScope` before `import_model` shows the file picker. The scope installs the least-change listener, and the dialog hook answers the native picker with Cancel (5101) before it draws. The same reading applies to the ZIP contents chooser (`Plater.cpp:18519`), which is not yet run. This probably started with commit 3aa5a4435d (2026-11-03), which taught the hook to see native pickers. That date is an inference.
2. **Save-or-discard questions that contradict the 2026-09-29 ruling.** These are "Transfer or discard changes" in the settings window (`Tab.cpp:7818`), and the same dialog when Filament settings… is reopened after an edit (from reading only). Two more: JusPrin's own OrcaSlicer import window (`OrcaImportWindow.cpp:161`) and the Windows/Linux title-bar Save button, which writes a 3MF outside the version store.
3. **Messages that arrive later, unasked, and often name OrcaSlicer.** Examples: connect failed, Network Plug-in Restriction, login expired, "Please try updating OrcaSlicer", failed to start print job, error uploading to print host, slice errors shown as a modal, process settings reset after a printer switch, tips that point at the hidden per-object settings panel. Most of the printer ones pass through two places in `GUI_App.cpp`. One is the `EVT_SHOW_DIALOG` handler, which `show_dialog` and `push_notification` both feed (connect failed, `DeviceManager`, `TaskManager`). The other is `process_network_msg` (the plug-in messages).
4. **Keys and menu paths that skip JusPrin.** Ctrl+Shift+E publishes a 3MF. Ctrl+G exports a sliced file. Ctrl+Shift+G prints without JusPrin's printer-connection check. All gizmo keys and the whole right-click menu still work.
5. **Popups the dialog hook cannot see.** These are shown with `Show()`, not `ShowModal()`: `DeviceErrorDialog` after any command sent to a Bambu printer, the stop-print confirm, the firmware prompts, and the chamber-temperature warning on macOS. Most live inside the monitor window, which embeds OrcaSlicer's whole Device page.

## Witness runs

"""Build the inventory page from rows.json and the inventory files' "not traced" notes.

Usage: python3 -I build_page.py <inventory dir> <rows.json> <template> <out.html>
"""
import json, re, sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
SURFACES = {
    "menus-and-app": "Menus, keys, startup and quit",
    "settings-window": "OrcaSlicer's settings window",
    "canvas": "Prepare canvas and Check print",
    "printers-and-devices": "Printers, monitor, print and send",
    "hidden-pages-and-keys": "Hidden pages and other keys",
    "preferences-and-notice-links": "OrcaSlicer Preferences and notice links",
    "popups-outside-the-hook": "Popups the dialog hook cannot see",
    "side-paths": "Setup wizard and other side paths",
    "jusprin-own-dialogs": "JusPrin's own dialogs",
}
KEYS = ("not traced", "not searched", "only skimmed", "did not trace")


def gaps_of(text):
    out, collecting = [], False
    for line in text.splitlines():
        s = line.strip()
        low = s.lower()
        is_bullet = bool(re.match(r"^([-*]|\d+\.)\s", s))
        starts_gap = any(k in low for k in KEYS) and (s.startswith("#") or not is_bullet or s.startswith("- **"))
        if starts_gap:
            collecting = True
            # A note that carries its content on the same line, after a colon.
            m = re.search(r":\*{0,2}\s*(.+)$", s)
            if m and not s.startswith("#") and len(m.group(1)) > 20:
                out.append(re.sub(r"^\*+|\*+$", "", s.lstrip("-* ")).strip())
            continue
        if collecting:
            if is_bullet:
                out.append(re.sub(r"^([-*]|\d+\.)\s+", "", s))
            elif s.startswith("#") or (s and not line.startswith(" ")):
                collecting = False
    return out


def main():
    d, rows_path, tpl, out = map(Path, sys.argv[1:5])
    rows = json.loads(rows_path.read_text())
    gaps_file = rows_path.parent / "gaps.json"
    gaps = json.loads(gaps_file.read_text()) if gaps_file.exists() else {}
    live = [r for r in rows if r["reach"] in ("yes", "answered", "unsure")]
    lede = (
        f"Every dialog OrcaSlicer code can show while the JusPrin view is on screen, plus JusPrin's own. "
        f"I found them by reading jusprin-dev at `cccef9f228`, and by running the shell harness with its dialog witness, which records each dialog that reaches the screen. "
        f"There are {len(rows)} rows, and {len(live)} of them can reach a person in the JusPrin view. "
        f"A few dialogs appear under two headings, because they can be reached from two places. "
        f"**Every route is a proposal. You have agreed to none of them.** "
        f"Click a coloured box to filter by route. Each row says what the dialog says, when it appears, why I think it can be reached, and the route I propose."
    )
    findings = [
        ["run", "In an open project, File › Import 3MF/STL… and Ctrl/Cmd+I import nothing. JusPrin's automatic answers for the file open start before the file picker opens, so the picker is cancelled before it draws."],
        ["read", "The ZIP contents chooser, for an imported or dropped .zip, opens under the same automatic answers, so I'd expect it to be cancelled the same way."],
        ["read", "Choosing \"Open existing project\" for a file opened before, when that open then fails: the \"Couldn't open project\" message opens under the same automatic answers, so I'd expect it to close before it is seen."],
        ["read", "After a print is sent to a Bambu printer, OrcaSlicer switches the main window to its Device page, and the JusPrin view shows it under JusPrin's header. Nothing in JusPrin catches this switch."],
        ["read", "Ctrl+Tab steps through OrcaSlicer's hidden pages (Preview, Device, Project, Calibration) in the JusPrin view. Entering Preview starts a slice and can ask to sync nozzle and AMS information."],
        ["read", "Besides the header printer menu, several JusPrin paths can still show OrcaSlicer's \"Transfer or discard changes\": rename, remove or open the settings of a printer that is not selected on Home, starting calibration from a Home card, reopening Filament settings… after an edit, and importing printers from OrcaSlicer."],
    ]
    html = tpl.read_text()
    html = html.replace("/*DATA*/[]", json.dumps(rows, ensure_ascii=False).replace("</", "<\\/"))
    html = html.replace("/*GAPS*/{}", json.dumps(gaps, ensure_ascii=False).replace("</", "<\\/"))
    html = html.replace("/*META*/{}", json.dumps({"lede": lede, "findings": findings}, ensure_ascii=False).replace("</", "<\\/"))
    html = html.replace("</script>", "</script>", 1)
    out.write_text(html)
    print(len(rows), "rows,", len(live), "live,", sum(len(v) for v in gaps.values()), "gap notes in", len(gaps), "files")


main()

# OrcaSlicer dialogs in the JusPrin view: inventory, 2026-11-18

This folder lists every modal dialog OrcaSlicer can open while the JusPrin view is showing. It was built by reading the code at jusprin-dev `cccef9f228` and by running 17 shell-harness modes with the dialog witness. Each dialog has a proposed route. **Every route is a proposal. Kenneth has agreed to none of them.**

Routes:
- **SHOW**: the person just asked for this, so OrcaSlicer's dialog is the right answer. Examples: a file picker, a delete confirmation, the send dialog.
- **JUSPRIN-MESSAGE**: the fact matters, but it should reach the person through JusPrin's own UI, because the dialog arrives unasked, names OrcaSlicer, or points at UI the JusPrin view hides.
- **ANSWER**: JusPrin answers it automatically. Used for save-or-discard questions, which the 2026-09-29 ruling replaces with autosave plus version history.
- **DROP**: the dialog, or the key or button that leads to it, should not be reachable.
- **UNSURE**: needs a product decision. The row says what decides it.

## Files

| File | Surface | Rows | Reachable in the JusPrin view |
|---|---|---|---|
| `menus-and-app.md` | Menus, keyboard shortcuts, startup and quit | 31 | 26 |
| `settings-window.md` | OrcaSlicer's settings window (filament and printer tabs) | 36 | 27 |
| `canvas.md` | Prepare canvas, right-click menu, gizmo keys, left pane object and plate actions, slice and export | 66 | 53 |
| `printers-and-devices.md` | Printer connection, the monitor window, print and send | 62 | 54 |
| `witness-summary.md` | Dialogs the harness saw reach the screen | | |
| `jusprin-own-dialog-sites.txt` | JusPrin's own dialog call sites, for comparison | | |

Some dialogs appear on more than one surface (clone, delete part of a cut object, the export picker), so the totals overlap a little.

Approximate totals across the reachable rows: about 90 SHOW, about 45 JUSPRIN-MESSAGE, about 6 ANSWER, about 10 DROP, about 20 UNSURE.

## The groups that are actually a problem

1. **JusPrin's auto-answer cancels pickers the person asked for.** Verified in the harness: File › Import 3MF/STL… (and Ctrl/Cmd+I) in an open project imports nothing. `Plater::add_file` opens a `FileOpenScope` before `import_model` shows the file picker. The scope installs the least-change listener, and the dialog hook answers the native picker with Cancel (5101) before it draws. The same reading applies to the ZIP contents chooser (`Plater.cpp:18519`), which is not yet run. This probably started with commit 3aa5a4435d (2026-11-03), which taught the hook to see native pickers. That date is an inference.
2. **Save-or-discard questions that contradict the 2026-09-29 ruling.** These are "Transfer or discard changes" in the settings window (`Tab.cpp:7818`), and the same dialog when Filament settings… is reopened after an edit (from reading only). Two more: JusPrin's own OrcaSlicer import window (`OrcaImportWindow.cpp:161`) and the Windows/Linux title-bar Save button, which writes a 3MF outside the version store.
3. **Messages that arrive later, unasked, and often name OrcaSlicer.** Examples: connect failed, Network Plug-in Restriction, login expired, "Please try updating OrcaSlicer", failed to start print job, error uploading to print host, slice errors shown as a modal, process settings reset after a printer switch, tips that point at the hidden per-object settings panel. Most of the printer ones pass through two places in `GUI_App.cpp`. One is the `EVT_SHOW_DIALOG` handler, which `show_dialog` and `push_notification` both feed (connect failed, `DeviceManager`, `TaskManager`). The other is `process_network_msg` (the plug-in messages).
4. **Keys and menu paths that skip JusPrin.** Ctrl+Shift+E publishes a 3MF. Ctrl+G exports a sliced file. Ctrl+Shift+G prints without JusPrin's printer-connection check. All gizmo keys and the whole right-click menu still work.
5. **Popups the dialog hook cannot see.** These are shown with `Show()`, not `ShowModal()`: `DeviceErrorDialog` after any command sent to a Bambu printer, the stop-print confirm, the firmware prompts, and the chamber-temperature warning on macOS. Most live inside the monitor window, which embeds OrcaSlicer's whole Device page.

"""Build the inventory page from rows.json and the inventory files' "not traced" notes.

Usage: python3 -I build_page.py <inventory dir> <rows.json> <template> <out.html>
"""
import json, re, sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
SURFACES = {
    "menus-and-app": "Menus, keys, startup and quit",
    "settings-window": "OrcaSlicer's settings window",
    "canvas": "Prepare canvas and Check print",
    "printers-and-devices": "Printers, monitor, print and send",
    "hidden-pages-and-keys": "Hidden pages and other keys",
    "preferences-and-notice-links": "OrcaSlicer Preferences and notice links",
    "popups-outside-the-hook": "Popups the dialog hook cannot see",
    "side-paths": "Setup wizard and other side paths",
    "jusprin-own-dialogs": "JusPrin's own dialogs",
}
KEYS = ("not traced", "not searched", "only skimmed", "did not trace")


def gaps_of(text):
    out, collecting = [], False
    for line in text.splitlines():
        s = line.strip()
        low = s.lower()
        is_bullet = bool(re.match(r"^([-*]|\d+\.)\s", s))
        starts_gap = any(k in low for k in KEYS) and (s.startswith("#") or not is_bullet or s.startswith("- **"))
        if starts_gap:
            collecting = True
            # A note that carries its content on the same line, after a colon.
            m = re.search(r":\*{0,2}\s*(.+)$", s)
            if m and not s.startswith("#") and len(m.group(1)) > 20:
                out.append(re.sub(r"^\*+|\*+$", "", s.lstrip("-* ")).strip())
            continue
        if collecting:
            if is_bullet:
                out.append(re.sub(r"^([-*]|\d+\.)\s+", "", s))
            elif s.startswith("#") or (s and not line.startswith(" ")):
                collecting = False
    return out


def main():
    d, rows_path, tpl, out = map(Path, sys.argv[1:5])
    rows = json.loads(rows_path.read_text())
    gaps_file = rows_path.parent / "gaps.json"
    gaps = json.loads(gaps_file.read_text()) if gaps_file.exists() else {}
    live = [r for r in rows if r["reach"] in ("yes", "answered", "unsure")]
    lede = (
        f"Every dialog OrcaSlicer code can show while the JusPrin view is on screen, plus JusPrin's own. "
        f"I found them by reading jusprin-dev at `cccef9f228`, and by running the shell harness with its dialog witness, which records each dialog that reaches the screen. "
        f"There are {len(rows)} rows, and {len(live)} of them can reach a person in the JusPrin view. "
        f"A few dialogs appear under two headings, because they can be reached from two places. "
        f"**Every route is a proposal. You have agreed to none of them.** "
        f"Click a coloured box to filter by route. Each row says what the dialog says, when it appears, why I think it can be reached, and the route I propose."
    )
    findings = [
        ["run", "In an open project, File › Import 3MF/STL… and Ctrl/Cmd+I import nothing. JusPrin's automatic answers for the file open start before the file picker opens, so the picker is cancelled before it draws."],
        ["read", "The ZIP contents chooser, for an imported or dropped .zip, opens under the same automatic answers, so I'd expect it to be cancelled the same way."],
        ["read", "Choosing \"Open existing project\" for a file opened before, when that open then fails: the \"Couldn't open project\" message opens under the same automatic answers, so I'd expect it to close before it is seen."],
        ["read", "After a print is sent to a Bambu printer, OrcaSlicer switches the main window to its Device page, and the JusPrin view shows it under JusPrin's header. Nothing in JusPrin catches this switch."],
        ["read", "Ctrl+Tab steps through OrcaSlicer's hidden pages (Preview, Device, Project, Calibration) in the JusPrin view. Entering Preview starts a slice and can ask to sync nozzle and AMS information."],
        ["read", "Besides the header printer menu, several JusPrin paths can still show OrcaSlicer's \"Transfer or discard changes\": rename, remove or open the settings of a printer that is not selected on Home, starting calibration from a Home card, reopening Filament settings… after an edit, and importing printers from OrcaSlicer."],
    ]
    html = tpl.read_text()
    html = html.replace("/*DATA*/[]", json.dumps(rows, ensure_ascii=False).replace("</", "<\\/"))
    html = html.replace("/*GAPS*/{}", json.dumps(gaps, ensure_ascii=False).replace("</", "<\\/"))
    html = html.replace("/*META*/{}", json.dumps({"lede": lede, "findings": findings}, ensure_ascii=False).replace("</", "<\\/"))
    html = html.replace("</script>", "</script>", 1)
    out.write_text(html)
    print(len(rows), "rows,", len(live), "live,", sum(len(v) for v in gaps.values()), "gap notes in", len(gaps), "files")


main()

# OrcaSlicer dialogs in the JusPrin view: inventory, 2026-11-18

This folder lists every modal dialog OrcaSlicer can open while the JusPrin view is showing. It was built by reading the code at jusprin-dev `cccef9f228` and by running 17 shell-harness modes with the dialog witness. Each dialog has a proposed route. **Every route is a proposal. Kenneth has agreed to none of them.**

Routes:
- **SHOW**: the person just asked for this, so OrcaSlicer's dialog is the right answer. Examples: a file picker, a delete confirmation, the send dialog.
- **JUSPRIN-MESSAGE**: the fact matters, but it should reach the person through JusPrin's own UI, because the dialog arrives unasked, names OrcaSlicer, or points at UI the JusPrin view hides.
- **ANSWER**: JusPrin answers it automatically. Used for save-or-discard questions, which the 2026-09-29 ruling replaces with autosave plus version history.
- **DROP**: the dialog, or the key or button that leads to it, should not be reachable.
- **UNSURE**: needs a product decision. The row says what decides it.

## Files

| File | Surface | Rows | Reachable in the JusPrin view |
|---|---|---|---|
| `menus-and-app.md` | Menus, keyboard shortcuts, startup and quit | 31 | 26 |
| `settings-window.md` | OrcaSlicer's settings window (filament and printer tabs) | 36 | 27 |
| `canvas.md` | Prepare canvas, right-click menu, gizmo keys, left pane object and plate actions, slice and export | 66 | 53 |
| `printers-and-devices.md` | Printer connection, the monitor window, print and send | 62 | 54 |
| `witness-summary.md` | Dialogs the harness saw reach the screen | | |
| `jusprin-own-dialog-sites.txt` | JusPrin's own dialog call sites, for comparison | | |

Some dialogs appear on more than one surface (clone, delete part of a cut object, the export picker), so the totals overlap a little.

Approximate totals across the reachable rows: about 90 SHOW, about 45 JUSPRIN-MESSAGE, about 6 ANSWER, about 10 DROP, about 20 UNSURE.

## The groups that are actually a problem

1. **JusPrin's auto-answer cancels pickers the person asked for.** Verified in the harness: File › Import 3MF/STL… (and Ctrl/Cmd+I) in an open project imports nothing. `Plater::add_file` opens a `FileOpenScope` before `import_model` shows the file picker. The scope installs the least-change listener, and the dialog hook answers the native picker with Cancel (5101) before it draws. The same reading applies to the ZIP contents chooser (`Plater.cpp:18519`), which is not yet run. This probably started with commit 3aa5a4435d (2026-11-03), which taught the hook to see native pickers. That date is an inference.
2. **Save-or-discard questions that contradict the 2026-09-29 ruling.** These are "Transfer or discard changes" in the settings window (`Tab.cpp:7818`), and the same dialog when Filament settings… is reopened after an edit (from reading only). Two more: JusPrin's own OrcaSlicer import window (`OrcaImportWindow.cpp:161`) and the Windows/Linux title-bar Save button, which writes a 3MF outside the version store.
3. **Messages that arrive later, unasked, and often name OrcaSlicer.** Examples: connect failed, Network Plug-in Restriction, login expired, "Please try updating OrcaSlicer", failed to start print job, error uploading to print host, slice errors shown as a modal, process settings reset after a printer switch, tips that point at the hidden per-object settings panel. Most of the printer ones pass through two places in `GUI_App.cpp`. One is the `EVT_SHOW_DIALOG` handler, which `show_dialog` and `push_notification` both feed (connect failed, `DeviceManager`, `TaskManager`). The other is `process_network_msg` (the plug-in messages).
4. **Keys and menu paths that skip JusPrin.** Ctrl+Shift+E publishes a 3MF. Ctrl+G exports a sliced file. Ctrl+Shift+G prints without JusPrin's printer-connection check. All gizmo keys and the whole right-click menu still work.
5. **Popups the dialog hook cannot see.** These are shown with `Show()`, not `ShowModal()`: `DeviceErrorDialog` after any command sent to a Bambu printer, the stop-print confirm, the firmware prompts, and the chamber-temperature warning on macOS. Most live inside the monitor window, which embeds OrcaSlicer's whole Device page.

## Witness runs

Of the OrcaSlicer dialogs that reached the screen in the harness, these are worth a look: "Send print job", "Material settings" (modeless), "Spiral mode only works when…" (titled "JusPrin info"), "Object too small … scale to millimeters?", and "Transfer or discard changes" (in the test case where the save fails).

The witness flag closes every dialog it sees. That changes what the code after the dialog does, so the witness runs' own failures in the mcp-setup, print-issue-readers, account-box and server-sheet modes are probably caused by the flag. That is a hypothesis, not checked against the same modes run without it.

"""Build the inventory page from rows.json and the inventory files' "not traced" notes.

Usage: python3 -I build_page.py <inventory dir> <rows.json> <template> <out.html>
"""
import json, re, sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
SURFACES = {
    "menus-and-app": "Menus, keys, startup and quit",
    "settings-window": "OrcaSlicer's settings window",
    "canvas": "Prepare canvas and Check print",
    "printers-and-devices": "Printers, monitor, print and send",
    "hidden-pages-and-keys": "Hidden pages and other keys",
    "preferences-and-notice-links": "OrcaSlicer Preferences and notice links",
    "popups-outside-the-hook": "Popups the dialog hook cannot see",
    "side-paths": "Setup wizard and other side paths",
    "jusprin-own-dialogs": "JusPrin's own dialogs",
}
KEYS = ("not traced", "not searched", "only skimmed", "did not trace")


def gaps_of(text):
    out, collecting = [], False
    for line in text.splitlines():
        s = line.strip()
        low = s.lower()
        is_bullet = bool(re.match(r"^([-*]|\d+\.)\s", s))
        starts_gap = any(k in low for k in KEYS) and (s.startswith("#") or not is_bullet or s.startswith("- **"))
        if starts_gap:
            collecting = True
            # A note that carries its content on the same line, after a colon.
            m = re.search(r":\*{0,2}\s*(.+)$", s)
            if m and not s.startswith("#") and len(m.group(1)) > 20:
                out.append(re.sub(r"^\*+|\*+$", "", s.lstrip("-* ")).strip())
            continue
        if collecting:
            if is_bullet:
                out.append(re.sub(r"^([-*]|\d+\.)\s+", "", s))
            elif s.startswith("#") or (s and not line.startswith(" ")):
                collecting = False
    return out


def main():
    d, rows_path, tpl, out = map(Path, sys.argv[1:5])
    rows = json.loads(rows_path.read_text())
    gaps_file = rows_path.parent / "gaps.json"
    gaps = json.loads(gaps_file.read_text()) if gaps_file.exists() else {}
    live = [r for r in rows if r["reach"] in ("yes", "answered", "unsure")]
    lede = (
        f"Every dialog OrcaSlicer code can show while the JusPrin view is on screen, plus JusPrin's own. "
        f"I found them by reading jusprin-dev at `cccef9f228`, and by running the shell harness with its dialog witness, which records each dialog that reaches the screen. "
        f"There are {len(rows)} rows, and {len(live)} of them can reach a person in the JusPrin view. "
        f"A few dialogs appear under two headings, because they can be reached from two places. "
        f"**Every route is a proposal. You have agreed to none of them.** "
        f"Click a coloured box to filter by route. Each row says what the dialog says, when it appears, why I think it can be reached, and the route I propose."
    )
    findings = [
        ["run", "In an open project, File › Import 3MF/STL… and Ctrl/Cmd+I import nothing. JusPrin's automatic answers for the file open start before the file picker opens, so the picker is cancelled before it draws."],
        ["read", "The ZIP contents chooser, for an imported or dropped .zip, opens under the same automatic answers, so I'd expect it to be cancelled the same way."],
        ["read", "Choosing \"Open existing project\" for a file opened before, when that open then fails: the \"Couldn't open project\" message opens under the same automatic answers, so I'd expect it to close before it is seen."],
        ["read", "After a print is sent to a Bambu printer, OrcaSlicer switches the main window to its Device page, and the JusPrin view shows it under JusPrin's header. Nothing in JusPrin catches this switch."],
        ["read", "Ctrl+Tab steps through OrcaSlicer's hidden pages (Preview, Device, Project, Calibration) in the JusPrin view. Entering Preview starts a slice and can ask to sync nozzle and AMS information."],
        ["read", "Besides the header printer menu, several JusPrin paths can still show OrcaSlicer's \"Transfer or discard changes\": rename, remove or open the settings of a printer that is not selected on Home, starting calibration from a Home card, reopening Filament settings… after an edit, and importing printers from OrcaSlicer."],
    ]
    html = tpl.read_text()
    html = html.replace("/*DATA*/[]", json.dumps(rows, ensure_ascii=False).replace("</", "<\\/"))
    html = html.replace("/*GAPS*/{}", json.dumps(gaps, ensure_ascii=False).replace("</", "<\\/"))
    html = html.replace("/*META*/{}", json.dumps({"lede": lede, "findings": findings}, ensure_ascii=False).replace("</", "<\\/"))
    html = html.replace("</script>", "</script>", 1)
    out.write_text(html)
    print(len(rows), "rows,", len(live), "live,", sum(len(v) for v in gaps.values()), "gap notes in", len(gaps), "files")


main()

=== d0bce03db3
d0bce03db37575117c5eba34d684c49a3370c9bd
2026-10-12
Show OrcaSlicer's notifications in JusPrin's own way: print issues, confirmations, and work in the chat

Inside the JusPrin shell OrcaSlicer's own pop-up notifications are held but
no longer drawn. JusPrin reads the list back and draws what it holds:

- Print problems: a status in the lower right corner of the Prepare canvas,
  shown only while there is an issue, the list it opens, and a bubble beside
  the object the selected issue is about, with Ask AI and Resolve with AI.
- The outcome of an action (export finished, an arrange that was refused): a
  short confirmation above the status, with a close button that closes
  OrcaSlicer's own notification.
- Work that is still running (a slice, an arrange, an export): an entry in
  the chat with a progress bar and, where the work can be stopped, Cancel.

This is two commits from feature-popup-message-handling as one: the first
print-issues design (6394191523), which was taken off this branch for a
rethink, and the redesign that followed (0c3bbcce42).

OrcaSlicer's notification list is the source of truth. PrintIssues/NoticeKinds
routes each of its 62 notification kinds: print problem, outcome of an
action, running work, application state, or not shown. Every kind is named
in one of five lists, and a kind OrcaSlicer adds stops the build in that
file until someone routes it. A print-problem notification becomes an issue
in OrcaSlicer's words. A notification carries no object, so where OrcaSlicer
lets its check be asked again (validation, a copy over the plate's edge, an
object out of a nozzle's reach, a slicing step warning) the check is asked
once more for the object only, and that entry exists only while OrcaSlicer
holds a notification of its kind. The rule is issues_from in
PrintIssues/PrintIssue, plain data with its own tests. Nothing here decides
whether something is a problem.

Two things are read whether or not a notification exists. The slice result:
a path outside the plate, a filament its nozzle cannot reach and a filament
that cannot print on the plate surface get their notifications only when
Check print loads the slice, while OrcaSlicer refuses to print from the
moment the slice ends. And why a slice failed: a critical failure shows a
dialog and leaves no notification. It is read from EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED,
which Plater.cpp defines and no header declared; a fork header Plater.cpp
already includes declares it, with no OrcaSlicer line changed.

PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor is told to look again on the first line of
NotificationManager::update_notifications, compares cheaply, and rebuilds
only on a change. While OrcaSlicer holds an edit it has not yet applied to
the print, the issues are marked stale, the status says it is checking, and
the buttons are off. The status is drawn only while there is an issue, so
its going is the all-clear, and it never goes before a check.
Only the active plate is reported, because that is the only plate OrcaSlicer
checks. "Blocks printing" is OrcaSlicer's own answer, never a stricter test
of the fork's.

Canvas (PrintIssues/IssueOverlay, IssueOverlayLayout): drawn with ImGui
through the overlay hook the tool strip uses. The bubble goes above its
object, else right, left or below, and never covers the object, the status,
the open list, a confirmation or the tool strip. It docks beside the status
for a plate-wide issue or an object out of view. Its pager walks every
issue. Selecting an issue selects its copy by OrcaSlicer's own id.

Closing hides and never resolves; the status is the way back, and the list
and the bubble are open one at a time. The list closes on a pick, a second
press of the status, Escape, or a press outside it. The bubble belongs to
the selection: it closes when its object stops being selected, which is what
a click on the empty plate, Escape and a click on another object already do
in OrcaSlicer, and stays open while the view is turned or the object is
dragged. Its close button leaves the selection alone, and a press on Ask AI
or Resolve with AI that reaches the chat closes it. With one issue the
status opens the bubble directly. Escape and presses are heard through
handlers of the fork's own on the canvas's window, bound after OrcaSlicer's
and so called first; no OrcaSlicer file is involved.

"Ignore this warning" in the bubble is the person's mark, not OrcaSlicer's
(mark_ignored in PrintIssues/PrintIssue, PrintIssueMonitor::set_ignored).
OrcaSlicer's notification is left alone: closing it would bring the warning
back at the next edit and close every other warning of its kind. The warning
stays in the list, marked, below the ones that count, and the status stops
counting it ("1 warning ignored" when nothing else is left). A blocker
cannot be ignored. An ignore lasts while OrcaSlicer keeps reporting that
warning, through edits, a slice and a plate switch, and is forgotten when
OrcaSlicer stops, so a warning that comes back is shown again. It is not
=== 0f46943de2
0f46943de26eed506684dc62ff30737c6aa426ef
2026-10-13
Hand OrcaSlicer's edit-time questions to the agent as preview warnings

When a person changes certain settings in OrcaSlicer's settings panel,
OrcaSlicer asks a question first: "smooth timelapse needs a prime tower,
enable it?", "this will change the shape of your model, are you sure?",
"change the recommended support settings for you?". The code that asks is
Tab::on_value_change, which runs for one field at a time. The settings tools
apply a patch through Tab::load_config, which never runs it. Since the tools
were allowed to change every setting except a short blacklist (5dadfe2801),
a patch could change these settings and nobody was asked or told.

settings_preview_patch now returns one warning per question, with code
orca_question:

- key: the setting the question is about;
- message: the question as a person would read it, whole;
- suggestions: the values OrcaSlicer's Yes would set, as key=value,
  leaving out any that already hold;
- min and max, for layer height: the nozzles' limits.

The patch stays valid and applies as sent. The agent settles the question
one of three ways, which the tool description spells out: go ahead; go
ahead and tell the user; or ask the user first, when the answer is theirs
to give. Kenneth chose this on 2026-10-12 over refusing the change, holding
it for approval, or blacklisting the settings. A valid tool call already
starts at once, and a "the person agreed" field would only be the agent's
word.

The rules are forward_edit_questions in the new OrcaEditQuestions.hpp, a
copy of the conditions in Tab.cpp for the process, object, filament and
printer scopes: the prime tower with smooth timelapse, clumping detection
or precise Z height; print by object on a bed-slinger; the support
filaments; make_overhang_printable; sparse_infill_rotate_template; layer
height outside the nozzles' limits; the two long retraction switches. No
OrcaSlicer file changes. A question is raised only for a setting the patch
really changes, with its condition read from the values the patch leaves,
so a patch that sends the companion value with the change raises nothing,
and neither does a state a person chose earlier.

Each message is looked up in the translation catalog piece by piece, as
Tab.cpp does it. The English catalog rewords some of them, so the literal
in the source is not what a person sees.

Because the conditions are copied from a file upstream edits, the workspace
adapter harness holds the copy to the original. It puts each value in the
tab's config the way a field does, runs OrcaSlicer's own handler with every
dialog answered and written down, and compares those dialogs with what
preview forwarded. verify_edit_questions does this for 27 cases, including
the ones that must raise nothing. verify_every_writable_setting does it for
every setting it applies, so a question upstream adds, drops or rewords
fails the sweep with the setting's name.

A warning or issue message may now be 2048 bytes in a tool result, up from
256, so that a whole question fits.

Tested on macOS, Release build:
- over real MCP on the shell harness fixture, a patch of timelapse_type=1,
  enable_prime_tower=0 and make_overhang_printable=1 returned no warnings
  with the call to the rules removed, and three orca_question warnings
  with it; it applied in both; adding the prime tower removed the
  timelapse warning;
- workspace adapter harness: 5913 checks pass. With the call removed, 37
  fail and the sweep names precise_z_height, make_overhang_printable and
  long_retractions_when_cut. With one question reworded on purpose,
  exactly one check fails;
- shell harness 550 checks, agent tests 281 cases, workspace contract
  tests 41 cases: all pass.

Not covered: how well a model chooses among the three is unmeasured. An
object override is checked at preview only. What on_value_change does
without asking (flush volumes after a long retraction switch,
filament_diameter and pellet_flow_coefficient kept in step,
thumbnails_format from thumbnails) is still skipped by a patch; the guide
lists these as undecided.

tests/printer_prompt/printer_tools.json is regenerated for the new tool
description.

=== 336facf825
336facf825305eab9876e21719d98b0081d4ce23
2026-10-14
No save-or-discard prompts; ask only about files opened before

On 2026-09-29 Kenneth decided JusPrin never asks a person to save or
discard: autosave keeps the work and version history is the way back.
Several paths still refused or asked. This brings them in line, and makes
the one question that remains, about a file opened before, consistent.

Save or discard:
- project_open releases the project through new_project, whose autosave
  hook saves it first; a failed save is the tool error. unsavedWork and the
  refusal are gone. Edited presets are dropped after the save.
- printer_setup drops unsaved preset edits and lists them in discarded;
  unsavedEdits and its refusal are gone.
- Saving another filament drops the open filament's unsaved edits and
  warns discards_unsaved_edits instead of refusing.
- Plater::load_project no longer stops opening a file over unsaved changes.
  That check fired even with autosave running, because autosave never
  resets Orca's own save tracker. Its prompt-table row is gone.
- A printer's nozzle change on the project's printer changes only after
  the unsaved edits are saved to version history; otherwise nothing
  changes. The printer panel's agent saves a version before printer_change,
  which lists the dropped keys in discarded.
- Connecting a printer keeps the project's other unsaved edits; renaming a
  printer no longer raises Orca's prompt and keeps the edits unsaved.

Skipped confirmations:
- orca_question is renamed skipped_confirmation (SkippedConfirmations.hpp):
  a confirmation OrcaSlicer asks of a person who makes a change, or saves
  it, by hand, which a patch skips. The save-time first-layer temperature
  check is now one of them instead of a refusal.

Files opened before:
- The "Previously opened file" question runs in Plater::load_project, so
  every way a person opens a .3mf asks. Each version records the file the
  project came from and its MD5; a changed file defaults to a new project.
  The agent's project_open returns opened_before and takes openedBefore.
- The question uses OrcaSlicer's MessageDialog, not a system alert. A
  dialog listener may return kShowToPerson to let one dialog through to
  the person while a file open answers the rest. Recorded as a lesson in
  the OrcaSlicer integration guide.

Harness checks cover each path; --reopen-prompt draws the dialog to PNGs.

- Print problems: a status in the lower right corner of the Prepare canvas,

  the object the selected issue is about, with Ask AI and Resolve with AI.

This is two commits from feature-popup-message-handling as one: the first
print-issues design (6394191523), which was taken off this branch for a
rethink, and the redesign that followed (0c3bbcce42).

OrcaSlicer's notification list is the source of truth. PrintIssues/NoticeKinds
routes each of its 62 notification kinds: print problem, outcome of an
action, running work, application state, or not shown. Every kind is named
in one of five lists, and a kind OrcaSlicer adds stops the build in that
file until someone routes it. A print-problem notification becomes an issue
in OrcaSlicer's words. A notification carries no object, so where OrcaSlicer
lets its check be asked again (validation, a copy over the plate's edge, an
object out of a nozzle's reach, a slicing step warning) the check is asked
once more for the object only, and that entry exists only while OrcaSlicer
holds a notification of its kind. The rule is issues_from in
PrintIssues/PrintIssue, plain data with its own tests. Nothing here decides
whether something is a problem.

Two things are read whether or not a notification exists. The slice result:
a path outside the plate, a filament its nozzle cannot reach and a filament
that cannot print on the plate surface get their notifications only when
Check print loads the slice, while OrcaSlicer refuses to print from the
moment the slice ends. And why a slice failed: a critical failure shows a
dialog and leaves no notification. It is read from EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED,
which Plater.cpp defines and no header declared; a fork header Plater.cpp
already includes declares it, with no OrcaSlicer line changed.

PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor is told to look again on the first line of
NotificationManager::update_notifications, compares cheaply, and rebuilds
only on a change. While OrcaSlicer holds an edit it has not yet applied to
the print, the issues are marked stale, the status says it is checking, and
the buttons are off. The status is drawn only while there is an issue, so
its going is the all-clear, and it never goes before a check.
Only the active plate is reported, because that is the only plate OrcaSlicer
checks. "Blocks printing" is OrcaSlicer's own answer, never a stricter test
of the fork's.

Canvas (PrintIssues/IssueOverlay, IssueOverlayLayout): drawn with ImGui
through the overlay hook the tool strip uses. The bubble goes above its
object, else right, left or below, and never covers the object, the status,
the open list, a confirmation or the tool strip. It docks beside the status
for a plate-wide issue or an object out of view. Its pager walks every
issue. Selecting an issue selects its copy by OrcaSlicer's own id.

and the bubble are open one at a time. The list closes on a pick, a second
press of the status, Escape, or a press outside it. The bubble belongs to

2026-10-13
Hand OrcaSlicer's edit-time questions to the agent as preview warnings

When a person changes certain settings in OrcaSlicer's settings panel,
OrcaSlicer asks a question first: "smooth timelapse needs a prime tower,
enable it?", "this will change the shape of your model, are you sure?",
"change the recommended support settings for you?". The code that asks is
Tab::on_value_change, which runs for one field at a time. The settings tools
apply a patch through Tab::load_config, which never runs it. Since the tools
were allowed to change every setting except a short blacklist (5dadfe2801),
a patch could change these settings and nobody was asked or told.

settings_preview_patch now returns one warning per question, with code
orca_question:

- key: the setting the question is about;
- message: the question as a person would read it, whole;
- suggestions: the values OrcaSlicer's Yes would set, as key=value,
  leaving out any that already hold;
- min and max, for layer height: the nozzles' limits.

The patch stays valid and applies as sent. The agent settles the question
one of three ways, which the tool description spells out: go ahead; go
ahead and tell the user; or ask the user first, when the answer is theirs
to give. Kenneth chose this on 2026-10-12 over refusing the change, holding
it for approval, or blacklisting the settings. A valid tool call already
starts at once, and a "the person agreed" field would only be the agent's
word.

The rules are forward_edit_questions in the new OrcaEditQuestions.hpp, a
copy of the conditions in Tab.cpp for the process, object, filament and
printer scopes: the prime tower with smooth timelapse, clumping detection
or precise Z height; print by object on a bed-slinger; the support
filaments; make_overhang_printable; sparse_infill_rotate_template; layer
height outside the nozzles' limits; the two long retraction switches. No
OrcaSlicer file changes. A question is raised only for a setting the patch
really changes, with its condition read from the values the patch leaves,
so a patch that sends the companion value with the change raises nothing,
and neither does a state a person chose earlier.

Each message is looked up in the translation catalog piece by piece, as
Tab.cpp does it. The English catalog rewords some of them, so the literal
in the source is not what a person sees.

Because the conditions are copied from a file upstream edits, the workspace
adapter harness holds the copy to the original. It puts each value in the
tab's config the way a field does, runs OrcaSlicer's own handler with every
dialog answered and written down, and compares those dialogs with what
preview forwarded. verify_edit_questions does this for 27 cases, including
the ones that must raise nothing. verify_every_writable_setting does it for
every setting it applies, so a question upstream adds, drops or rewords
fails the sweep with the setting's name.

A warning or issue message may now be 2048 bytes in a tool result, up from
256, so that a whole question fits.

=== d0bce03db3
d0bce03db37575117c5eba34d684c49a3370c9bd
2026-10-12
Show OrcaSlicer's notifications in JusPrin's own way: print issues, confirmations, and work in the chat

Inside the JusPrin shell OrcaSlicer's own pop-up notifications are held but
no longer drawn. JusPrin reads the list back and draws what it holds:

- Print problems: a status in the lower right corner of the Prepare canvas,
  shown only while there is an issue, the list it opens, and a bubble beside
  the object the selected issue is about, with Ask AI and Resolve with AI.
- The outcome of an action (export finished, an arrange that was refused): a
  short confirmation above the status, with a close button that closes
  OrcaSlicer's own notification.
- Work that is still running (a slice, an arrange, an export): an entry in
  the chat with a progress bar and, where the work can be stopped, Cancel.

This is two commits from feature-popup-message-handling as one: the first
print-issues design (6394191523), which was taken off this branch for a
rethink, and the redesign that followed (0c3bbcce42).

OrcaSlicer's notification list is the source of truth. PrintIssues/NoticeKinds
routes each of its 62 notification kinds: print problem, outcome of an
action, running work, application state, or not shown. Every kind is named
in one of five lists, and a kind OrcaSlicer adds stops the build in that
file until someone routes it. A print-problem notification becomes an issue
in OrcaSlicer's words. A notification carries no object, so where OrcaSlicer
lets its check be asked again (validation, a copy over the plate's edge, an
object out of a nozzle's reach, a slicing step warning) the check is asked
once more for the object only, and that entry exists only while OrcaSlicer
holds a notification of its kind. The rule is issues_from in
PrintIssues/PrintIssue, plain data with its own tests. Nothing here decides
whether something is a problem.

Two things are read whether or not a notification exists. The slice result:
a path outside the plate, a filament its nozzle cannot reach and a filament
that cannot print on the plate surface get their notifications only when
Check print loads the slice, while OrcaSlicer refuses to print from the
moment the slice ends. And why a slice failed: a critical failure shows a
dialog and leaves no notification. It is read from EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED,
which Plater.cpp defines and no header declared; a fork header Plater.cpp
already includes declares it, with no OrcaSlicer line changed.

PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor is told to look again on the first line of
NotificationManager::update_notifications, compares cheaply, and rebuilds
only on a change. While OrcaSlicer holds an edit it has not yet applied to
the print, the issues are marked stale, the status says it is checking, and
the buttons are off. The status is drawn only while there is an issue, so
its going is the all-clear, and it never goes before a check.
Only the active plate is reported, because that is the only plate OrcaSlicer
checks. "Blocks printing" is OrcaSlicer's own answer, never a stricter test
of the fork's.

Canvas (PrintIssues/IssueOverlay, IssueOverlayLayout): drawn with ImGui
through the overlay hook the tool strip uses. The bubble goes above its
object, else right, left or below, and never covers the object, the status,
the open list, a confirmation or the tool strip. It docks beside the status
for a plate-wide issue or an object out of view. Its pager walks every
issue. Selecting an issue selects its copy by OrcaSlicer's own id.

Closing hides and never resolves; the status is the way back, and the list
and the bubble are open one at a time. The list closes on a pick, a second
press of the status, Escape, or a press outside it. The bubble belongs to
the selection: it closes when its object stops being selected, which is what
a click on the empty plate, Escape and a click on another object already do
in OrcaSlicer, and stays open while the view is turned or the object is
dragged. Its close button leaves the selection alone, and a press on Ask AI
or Resolve with AI that reaches the chat closes it. With one issue the
status opens the bubble directly. Escape and presses are heard through
handlers of the fork's own on the canvas's window, bound after OrcaSlicer's
and so called first; no OrcaSlicer file is involved.

"Ignore this warning" in the bubble is the person's mark, not OrcaSlicer's
(mark_ignored in PrintIssues/PrintIssue, PrintIssueMonitor::set_ignored).
OrcaSlicer's notification is left alone: closing it would bring the warning
back at the next edit and close every other warning of its kind. The warning
stays in the list, marked, below the ones that count, and the status stops
counting it ("1 warning ignored" when nothing else is left). A blocker
cannot be ignored. An ignore lasts while OrcaSlicer keeps reporting that
warning, through edits, a slice and a plate switch, and is forgotten when
OrcaSlicer stops, so a warning that comes back is shown again. It is not
=== 0f46943de2
0f46943de26eed506684dc62ff30737c6aa426ef
2026-10-13
Hand OrcaSlicer's edit-time questions to the agent as preview warnings

When a person changes certain settings in OrcaSlicer's settings panel,
OrcaSlicer asks a question first: "smooth timelapse needs a prime tower,
enable it?", "this will change the shape of your model, are you sure?",
"change the recommended support settings for you?". The code that asks is
Tab::on_value_change, which runs for one field at a time. The settings tools
apply a patch through Tab::load_config, which never runs it. Since the tools
were allowed to change every setting except a short blacklist (5dadfe2801),
a patch could change these settings and nobody was asked or told.

settings_preview_patch now returns one warning per question, with code
orca_question:

- key: the setting the question is about;
- message: the question as a person would read it, whole;
- suggestions: the values OrcaSlicer's Yes would set, as key=value,
  leaving out any that already hold;
- min and max, for layer height: the nozzles' limits.

The patch stays valid and applies as sent. The agent settles the question
one of three ways, which the tool description spells out: go ahead; go
ahead and tell the user; or ask the user first, when the answer is theirs
to give. Kenneth chose this on 2026-10-12 over refusing the change, holding
it for approval, or blacklisting the settings. A valid tool call already
starts at once, and a "the person agreed" field would only be the agent's
word.

The rules are forward_edit_questions in the new OrcaEditQuestions.hpp, a
copy of the conditions in Tab.cpp for the process, object, filament and
printer scopes: the prime tower with smooth timelapse, clumping detection
or precise Z height; print by object on a bed-slinger; the support
filaments; make_overhang_printable; sparse_infill_rotate_template; layer
height outside the nozzles' limits; the two long retraction switches. No
OrcaSlicer file changes. A question is raised only for a setting the patch
really changes, with its condition read from the values the patch leaves,
so a patch that sends the companion value with the change raises nothing,
and neither does a state a person chose earlier.

Each message is looked up in the translation catalog piece by piece, as
Tab.cpp does it. The English catalog rewords some of them, so the literal
in the source is not what a person sees.

Because the conditions are copied from a file upstream edits, the workspace
adapter harness holds the copy to the original. It puts each value in the
tab's config the way a field does, runs OrcaSlicer's own handler with every
dialog answered and written down, and compares those dialogs with what
preview forwarded. verify_edit_questions does this for 27 cases, including
the ones that must raise nothing. verify_every_writable_setting does it for
every setting it applies, so a question upstream adds, drops or rewords
fails the sweep with the setting's name.

A warning or issue message may now be 2048 bytes in a tool result, up from
256, so that a whole question fits.

Tested on macOS, Release build:
- over real MCP on the shell harness fixture, a patch of timelapse_type=1,
  enable_prime_tower=0 and make_overhang_printable=1 returned no warnings
  with the call to the rules removed, and three orca_question warnings
  with it; it applied in both; adding the prime tower removed the
  timelapse warning;
- workspace adapter harness: 5913 checks pass. With the call removed, 37
  fail and the sweep names precise_z_height, make_overhang_printable and
  long_retractions_when_cut. With one question reworded on purpose,
  exactly one check fails;
- shell harness 550 checks, agent tests 281 cases, workspace contract
  tests 41 cases: all pass.

Not covered: how well a model chooses among the three is unmeasured. An
object override is checked at preview only. What on_value_change does
without asking (flush volumes after a long retraction switch,
filament_diameter and pellet_flow_coefficient kept in step,
thumbnails_format from thumbnails) is still skipped by a patch; the guide
lists these as undecided.

tests/printer_prompt/printer_tools.json is regenerated for the new tool
description.

=== 336facf825
336facf825305eab9876e21719d98b0081d4ce23
2026-10-14
No save-or-discard prompts; ask only about files opened before

On 2026-09-29 Kenneth decided JusPrin never asks a person to save or
discard: autosave keeps the work and version history is the way back.
Several paths still refused or asked. This brings them in line, and makes
the one question that remains, about a file opened before, consistent.

Save or discard:
- project_open releases the project through new_project, whose autosave
  hook saves it first; a failed save is the tool error. unsavedWork and the
  refusal are gone. Edited presets are dropped after the save.
- printer_setup drops unsaved preset edits and lists them in discarded;
  unsavedEdits and its refusal are gone.
- Saving another filament drops the open filament's unsaved edits and
  warns discards_unsaved_edits instead of refusing.
- Plater::load_project no longer stops opening a file over unsaved changes.
  That check fired even with autosave running, because autosave never
  resets Orca's own save tracker. Its prompt-table row is gone.
- A printer's nozzle change on the project's printer changes only after
  the unsaved edits are saved to version history; otherwise nothing
  changes. The printer panel's agent saves a version before printer_change,
  which lists the dropped keys in discarded.
- Connecting a printer keeps the project's other unsaved edits; renaming a
  printer no longer raises Orca's prompt and keeps the edits unsaved.

Skipped confirmations:
- orca_question is renamed skipped_confirmation (SkippedConfirmations.hpp):
  a confirmation OrcaSlicer asks of a person who makes a change, or saves
  it, by hand, which a patch skips. The save-time first-layer temperature
  check is now one of them instead of a refusal.

Files opened before:
- The "Previously opened file" question runs in Plater::load_project, so
  every way a person opens a .3mf asks. Each version records the file the
  project came from and its MD5; a changed file defaults to a new project.
  The agent's project_open returns opened_before and takes openedBefore.
- The question uses OrcaSlicer's MessageDialog, not a system alert. A
  dialog listener may return kShowToPerson to let one dialog through to
  the person while a file open answers the rest. Recorded as a lesson in
  the OrcaSlicer integration guide.

Harness checks cover each path; --reopen-prompt draws the dialog to PNGs.
